entries.title: First-Order Logic Course Guide
entries.header: Scope and conventions for the entire First-Order Logic branch.

entries.title: First-Order Signature
entries.header: Single-sorted classical first-order logic with logical equality.

entries.title: Terms
entries.header: Terms denote individuals; they are not formulas and have no truth value.

entries.title: Atomic Formulas and Formulas
entries.header: The grammar is fully parenthesized; other precedence conventions are abbreviations.

entries.title: Free and Bound Occurrences
entries.header: Freedom is a property of an occurrence, not merely of a variable symbol.

entries.title: Sentence, Theory, and Vocabulary
entries.header: A theory here is a set of sentences, not necessarily deductively closed.

entries.title: Restricted and Unique Quantification
entries.header: These are abbreviations inside ordinary first-order logic, not new quantifiers.

entries.title: Symbolize Nested Quantification
entries.header: Domain: people and books. $S(x)$ means “$x$ is a student”; $B(y)$ means “$y$ is a book”; $R(x,y)$ means “$x$ read $y$”.

entries.title: Capture-Avoiding Substitution
entries.header: Substitution replaces free occurrences only and must respect binding.

entries.title: Structural Induction for Terms and Formulas
entries.header: Applies to properties closed under every constructor in the grammar.

entries.title: Unique Readability
entries.header: Assumes disjoint symbol classes and the fully parenthesized grammar in this module.

entries.title: Parse Quantifier Scope
entries.header: Use the official grammar, not informal reading conventions.

entries.title: Prevent Variable Capture
entries.header: Substitute the term $y$ for the free variable $x$.

entries.title: First-Order Structure
entries.header: Domains are nonempty and every function symbol denotes a total function.

entries.title: Variable Assignment and Term Value
entries.header: Open terms and formulas require an assignment.

entries.title: Satisfaction Relation
entries.header: The relation $𝔐,g ⊨ φ$ is defined recursively on formulas.

entries.title: Truth, Model, and Satisfiability
entries.header: Truth of a sentence is assignment-independent.

entries.title: Semantic Consequence and Equivalence
entries.header: Semantic consequence quantifies over all structures and assignments.

entries.title: Coincidence Lemma
entries.header: Only values assigned to free variables can affect satisfaction.

entries.title: Semantic Substitution Lemma
entries.header: Assume $t$ is free for $x$ in $φ$.

entries.title: Isomorphism Invariance
entries.header: Isomorphisms preserve all symbols of the signature.

entries.title: Logical Equality Is Identity
entries.header: This course uses first-order logic with built-in equality.

entries.title: Refute a Quantifier Reversal
entries.header: Produce a concrete finite countermodel.

entries.title: Axiomatize Strict Linear Orders
entries.header: Language: one binary relation symbol $<$ with logical equality.

entries.title: Derivation and Syntactic Consequence
entries.header: Derivations are finite trees with explicitly discharged assumptions.

entries.title: Propositional Natural-Deduction Rules
entries.header: These rules act inside first-order derivations as well as propositional ones.

entries.title: Falsity and Classical Reasoning Rules
entries.header: Negation is treated as $φ→⊥$; reductio makes the system classical.

entries.title: Universal Quantifier Rules
entries.header: The eigenvariable side condition is essential.

entries.title: Existential Quantifier Rules
entries.header: Existential elimination introduces a genuinely fresh witness parameter.

entries.title: Equality Rules
entries.header: Equality introduction and elimination match semantic identity.

entries.title: Alpha-Renaming of Bound Variables
entries.header: Assume the new variable $y$ does not occur in $φ$.

entries.title: Weakening of Derivability
entries.header: Adding assumptions cannot destroy an existing derivation.

entries.title: Object Language, Metalanguage, and Side Conditions
entries.header: Do not turn metalinguistic restrictions into object-language premises.

entries.title: Derive a Valid Quantifier Distribution
entries.header: Assume $x$ is not free in $ψ$.

entries.title: Diagnose Invalid Quantifier Inferences
entries.header: For each invalid inference, identify the violated rule or give a countermodel.

entries.title: Derive Symmetry and Transitivity of Equality
entries.header: Use only equality introduction and substitution of identicals.

entries.title: Syntactic Consistency and Completeness of a Theory
entries.header: These are proof-theoretic notions; satisfiability is semantic.

entries.title: Local Soundness of Natural-Deduction Rules
entries.header: Each rule preserves semantic consequence relative to the open assumptions of its premise subderivations.

entries.title: Soundness Theorem
entries.header: For the classical natural-deduction system defined in this course.

entries.title: Finite Character of Derivability
entries.header: Natural-deduction derivations are finite objects.

entries.title: Lindenbaum Lemma
entries.header: For any set-sized first-order language; use a well-ordering of its sentences.

entries.title: Henkin Witness Property
entries.header: Witness constants belong to an expanded language.

entries.title: Henkin Extension Lemma
entries.header: For any set-sized language and consistent theory; uses fresh constants and well-ordering.

entries.title: Maximal Henkin Theory Lemma
entries.header: Combine Henkinization with maximal-consistent extension.

entries.title: Equality Congruence Lemma
entries.header: Let $Δ$ be a deductively closed consistent theory with equality.

entries.title: Quotient Term Model
entries.header: Built from a maximal Henkin theory $Δ$ with at least one closed term.

entries.title: Truth Lemma for the Henkin Model
entries.header: Let $Δ$ be maximal consistent, deductively closed, and Henkin.

entries.title: Model Existence Theorem
entries.header: For arbitrary set-sized first-order languages with logical equality.

entries.title: Gödel Completeness Theorem for First-Order Logic
entries.header: Strong completeness; first stated for a theory $Γ$ and a sentence $φ$.

entries.title: Compactness Theorem
entries.header: Semantic and consequence forms are both included.

entries.title: Substructure and Elementary Substructure
entries.header: Substructure preservation of atomic formulas is weaker than elementarity.

entries.title: Tarski–Vaught Test
entries.header: Let $𝔑$ be an $L$-substructure of $𝔐$.

entries.title: Downward Löwenheim–Skolem Theorem
entries.header: Cardinal form; assumes the usual set-theoretic choice needed to select witnesses.

entries.title: Upward Löwenheim–Skolem Theorem
entries.header: Assume $T$ has an infinite model and $κ≥\max(|L|,ℵ_0)$ is infinite.

entries.title: Construct a Nonstandard Model of Arithmetic
entries.header: Use compactness; do not claim the new model is the standard natural numbers.

entries.title: Compactness and the Limits of Finiteness
entries.header: First-order theories can force infinitude but cannot have exactly all finite structures as models.

entries.title: Skolem's Paradox and External Countability
entries.header: The apparent paradox dissolves by distinguishing internal from external viewpoints.

entries.title: Negation Normal Form
entries.header: Negations occur only immediately before an atomic formula or $⊥$.

entries.title: Negation Normal Form Theorem
entries.header: Classical first-order logic.

entries.title: Prenex Normal Form Theorem
entries.header: Bound variables must first be standardized apart.

entries.title: Skolemization
entries.header: Skolem symbols are new and record dependence on preceding universal variables.

entries.title: Skolem Equisatisfiability Theorem
entries.header: The conclusion is equisatisfiability, not logical equivalence; the forward direction uses choice of witnesses.

entries.title: Skolemization Is Not Equivalence
entries.header: Compare formulas in the expanded language.

entries.title: Effective Enumerability of First-Order Validity
entries.header: Assume a computable signature and an effective presentation of the proof rules.

entries.title: Church's Undecidability Boundary
entries.header: This entry states the boundary; a full reduction belongs in a computability course.

entries.title: Skolemize a Mixed Quantifier Prefix
entries.header: Keep every dependency on preceding universal variables.
